name: Exchangers rated from their geometry
description: U from film coefficients instead of a fixed number. A double-pipe exchanger (Kraume, Transportvorgänge in der Verfahrenstechnik, Example 5.12: 1 m³/h of water from 20 °C in a 50 mm steel tube, hot water from 60 °C in the 100 mm outer pipe, 45.9 m long) preheats the water; a steam-heated shell-and-tube heater (20 tubes of 19.05 mm in two passes) brings it to temperature; a stirred drum cools it again with cooling water in a helical coil (33.7 mm tube on a 0.9 m helix). Each unit reports its film coefficients, Reynolds and Nusselt numbers and the U they give, on the outer tube surface. Rate the drum with U_from jacket and a 25 mm jacket gap instead to see why plain jackets are poor: the cooling water creeps through the gap in laminar flow. Both water streams of the double pipe are in the transition region (Re 4400 and 9200), so U is low; shorten the outer pipe's diameter or raise the flows to see U rise. Give U again to compare with a fixed coefficient.
